speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the risks of airflow-related COVID-19 transmissibility at Changi Airport buildings given what we know about the Omicron variant transmission capabilities; and (b) what other enhanced measures can be taken to protect all our airport workers, both frontline and non-frontline.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how often does Changi Airport undergo studies of the presence, viability and infectivity of COVID-19 virus in its built environment, including in the air and on surfaces which members of the public or staff may come into contact with; (b) whether these studies are revisited when COVID-19 novel variants arise around the world with higher transmissibility, such as Delta and Omicron; and (c) when was this last studied.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport in light of the spread of the Omicron variant of COVID-19 (a) how does the Ministry review its border control measures for air travel with all countries as well as Vaccinated Travel Lane (VTL) and non-VTL travel with Malaysia, with the view to striking a meaningful balance between allowing travel to continue while minimising the risk of COVID-19 spread during travel; and (b) what measures can be expected from the Ministry in the coming weeks.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: asked the Minister for Transport with regard to the effort to jumpstart the Singapore economy in 2022 and to gain momentum in the aviation sector (a) whether the Ministry is taking any steps to ensure the continued growth and success of Singapore’s aviation industry; (b) if so, what are these steps; and (c) what are the additional efforts undertaken to ensure the success of the Singapore AirShow in 2022.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I will also address questions raised by Mr Seah Kian Peng1 and Mr Gan Thiam Poh for the Sittings on 11 and 12 January.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Dennis Tan have asked how we have reviewed our border measures in light of the Omicron variant, including what global and domestic indicators we monitor to inform our measures.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Essentially, it is a composite of both domestic and external factors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In September last year, with a substantial proportion of the Singapore population vaccinated, we launched the Vaccinated Travel Lanes (VTLs).

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Two months later, on 26 November, the World Health Organization (WHO) designated Omicron as a "Variant of Concern".

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Then, scientists around the world were still trying to ascertain Omicron's transmissibility and virulence relative to Delta and the efficacy of existing vaccines against this new variant.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Residents returning from these countries were subjected to a 10-day Stay-Home Notice (SHN) at dedicated facilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We halted the expansion of the VTL scheme and deferred the launch of the already-announced VTLs to Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We also decided to maintain the daily quota for VTL (Air) travellers at 10,000, rather than increase it to 15,000, as we had earlier intended.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan has asked whether this freeze was necessary, given our approach of living with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I have outlined, the freeze was part of a series of calibrated moves informed by the latest public health risk assessment as well as developments around the world.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It was essential to balance the need to manage the risk of imported Omicron cases while minimising disruption to travellers who had already made VTL bookings to enter Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ms Foo Mee Har had asked earlier about the breakdown of imported cases for Omicron.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This broadly corresponds to the VTL traveller volume and, as most Members will appreciate, it is also influenced by the incidence of Omicron in these countries.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would add that, of the composition of this figure, less than 10% were actually short-term visitors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, the bulk is actually Singapore Citizens (SCs), Permanent Residents (PRs) and long-term visit pass (LTVP) holders who are returning to Singapore from overseas.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ms Poh Li San, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the additional enhanced measures for VTL travellers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the first week of December 2021, in consultation with MOH, we introduced additional supervised self-administered antigen rapid tests (ARTs) for VTL travellers on Day Three and Day Seven after arrival.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is on top of the pre-departure and on-arrival test requirements.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: VTL travellers were also required to undergo self-administered ARTs on Days Two, Four, Five and Six of their arrival before going about their daily activities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Those who test positive are required to undergo a confirmatory PCR test.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, basically, pre-departure, on arrival and then from Day Two to Day Seven, there is daily ART self-administered, but on Days Three and Seven, they have to do it under supervision.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And these have to be reported and, if there is a positive ART result, then they go for a PCR test.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Collectively, these adjustments to our border and other measures have allowed us time to study and better understand the Omicron variant, to strengthen our defences, including our healthcare capacity, and to get more people vaccinated and boosted, as we have heard.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will continue to work closely with MOH to regularly review our border measures.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As part of learning to live with the virus and its variants, we must press on with our efforts to restore our connectivity with the world while safeguarding public health.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our goal is to restore quarantine-free travel with more countries and regions, as allowed for by the public health assessment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the additional measures to protect airport workers from Omicron.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Since 2 December 2021, we have enhanced the personal protective equipment (PPE) and testing protocols.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All frontline airport workers are now placed on a seven-day PCR Rostered Routine Testing (RRT) regime.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For higher-risk frontline airport workers, an employer-supervised ART was introduced on the third day in addition to their seven-day PCR RRT.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Further, all Singapore aircrew arriving from affected regions are required to undergo an on-arrival PCR test and post-arrival PCR tests on Days Three and Seven.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These protocols will be adjusted, as they have in the past, in accordance with the latest public health risk assessments.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about airflow and COVID-19 transmissibility at the airport.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Since the onset of the pandemic, Changi Airport Group (CAG) has progressively upgraded the air ventilation system at the airport.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For instance, CAG has upgraded the filters in the air-conditioning and mechanical ventilation (ACMV) system to Merv-14 filters, which are able to remove about 85% of particles of 0.3 to 1.0 micron in size.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, they can filter out particles smaller than the size of a respiratory particle containing the COVID-19 virus.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: With the emergence of the more transmissible Delta variant in May last year, CAAS, CAG, MOH, the National Environment Agency (NEA) and the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) conducted an airflow study to identify spaces at the airport where ventilation and filtration could be further stepped up.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These HEPA air purifiers are also used in hospitals, and they help to reduce the risk of airborne transmission of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Since September last year, CAG has also installed ultraviolet-C (UV-C) sanitation equipment in the airport terminal air-conditioning systems to provide an additional layer of defence.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Leon Perera, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Shawn Huang asked about upcoming VTL moves and the outlook for our air and maritime hubs in 2022.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Maritime businesses also continued to establish and expand operations here.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We expect the favourable outlook for trade and shipping to continue in 2022.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: According to industry projections, global seaborne trade is expected to grow 3.5% in 2022, slightly below the estimate of 3.6% last year.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are working with our tripartite partners to seize these opportunities, continue growing our maritime sector and create more good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the other hand, air travel is expected to take several years to recover to pre-pandemic levels.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Notwithstanding this, we remain confident of the long-term potential of air travel and are resolutely committed to working with Changi Airport Group and airline partners to rebuild and reclaim Singapore's status as an international air hub.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Therefore, barring unexpected setbacks like Omicron, we anticipate further recovery in 2022.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To Mr Leon Perera’s question, we do not restrict any airline from applying to operate VTL flights; the overall quota of inbound VTL travellers is allocated to airlines based on the plans they submit to CAAS.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Low-cost carriers, such as Scoot, AirAsia and Jetstar Asia, already operate VTL flights from Malaysia.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Scoot also operates VTL flights from Thailand and the Republic of Korea, Australia and Germany.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Perera also asked if we would allow more VTL flights during festive periods.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You have heard from the MTF and also in today's session in Parliament, we closely monitor the demand for VTL flights and will regularly review the VTL quotas, always taking into consideration the prevailing public health assessment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Shawn Huang asked about our plans for the Singapore Airshow in 2022.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Singapore Airshow is one of the world’s leading airshows that bring together aerospace and defence leaders and key decision makers to conduct business and forge partnerships.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The event organiser, Experia Events Pte Ltd, has announced that Singapore Airshow 2022 will go ahead from 15 to 18 February, for trade visitors only.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To ensure the success of Singapore Airshow 2022, our Government agencies are working closely with the organiser on the public health protocols to facilitate its safe and smooth execution, including ensuring the safe entry of international trade attendees and safe management measures at the event.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As part of living with COVID-19, we must shift to a new setting that will enable us to stay connected to the world.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is essential that we press on with our mission to reopen our borders.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The VTL scheme is a useful pathfinder for us to establish, test and build confidence in safe reopening to vaccinated travellers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ultimately, we want to work towards quarantine-free travel for all vaccinated travellers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Singapore’s global connectivity is critical to our economic competitiveness and the livelihoods of our people.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It underpins our status as an international business centre and global trading hub.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Over the past two years, the Government has provided significant support to preserve core capabilities in this strategic sector and to help them tide over this crisis.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will continue to work closely with our aviation stakeholders to rebuild a safe and sustainable Changi aviation hub.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My first supplementary question (SQ) is in relation to that.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And the Minister mentioned and elaborated on the aviation hub outlook.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share what are the risks of our regional partners trying to gain a foothold in our aviation sector in terms of its growth and hub status as well?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, I am heartened to hear that CAAS is working to improve the airport ventilation rates, especially in a built environment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But the airport phase is key and I hope we can continue to enhance the airport phase's cleanliness, filters and airflows.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question is in relation to transport passenger volume.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If we are going to grow it further forward, what measures can we take to enhance it even more because, definitely, with Changi Airport, we want to enhance the transit passenger volume even further as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, on the reports that he has cited, I do not think I can speak with authority on the specific plans that the Indonesian government or, for that matter, any other government or regional players have.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But let me start by saying that Changi is no stranger to competition.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have always had to compete with a whole variety of regional hubs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And there will continue to be new hubs that will emerge.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Therefore, it is critical that we work at the system level with all the partners – whether it is Changi Airport Group, airline partners, SATS and other ground handlers, the unions and, certainly, the Government agencies, including CAAS.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is important that we mount a systemic response to preserve our competitiveness as an international aviation hub.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Central to that, in terms of looking ahead, I think that it will be underpinned by two key factors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The first is to emerge from the COVID-19 pandemic in a manner that is safe and robust so that travellers, airlines and, indeed, the general population, have the confidence that air travel can, in fact, continue in a safe manner and that Changi is one of the places that they can travel through with utmost confidence.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, throughout the last 12 to 18 months, for all the airport players here in the aviation cluster, basically, it has been a Herculean effort because we have had to invert the operating model in Changi.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: A civilian airport, in general, is designed for an experience, for passengers to interact and we have had to reverse that logic and start to look at segmentation, testing and all kinds of other necessary protocols to protect health, but it means the travel experience is diminished.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But how much and how fast are really a function of the environment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And we need to always prioritise the public health assessment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would add that, beyond safe recovery, the longer-term competitive proposition of Changi will also rest on sustainability.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is something that CAAS is working on with all the partners.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That will also be an important competitive differentiator for us going forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is an effort that is currently being undertaken by MOT with CAAS and all our partners.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have an SQ for the Minister for Transport.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The Minister has spoken about what has been done to clean the air filtration better, to try and sterilise surfaces better with UVC.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But can I ask the Minister how are we evaluating the effectiveness of these measures?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Are we checking whether there is viral detectability in the ambient air?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Are we checking for detectable virus on surfaces that members of the public or members of staff may come into contact with?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And if I may put a second SQ to MOT, can the Minister confirm that there is ongoing attention to making sure that existing security protocols in the airport also interlink safely with safe management measures?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, for example, where staff are required to have their faces validated against photo IDs, that this is done in a way that does not undermine the safe management processes against COVID-19.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we have undertaken a whole series of steps to ensure that our workers are protected to the best of our ability.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is why I mentioned, specifically, the moves we have made with respect to personal protective equipment, or PPEs, and we have heightened them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would add that we have also the testing protocols that we have enhanced.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All of these, on the one hand, ensure a higher level of safety for our workers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I must also emphasise that it also means additional inconveniences and challenges.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I just wanted to highlight to Members – and I have been engaged in conversations with the union leaders and so on – that every one of these moves does impose a real human burden, which we have to take into account.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the first point on detection and how we continue to monitor, CAAS and Changi Airport are not the specialists in this area.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But they are fully committed to protecting the environment to the best of their ability.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In some ways, I think Changi Airport or its surrounding facilities are not too different from many commercial building settings and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This flow of people is from different sources and there are all kinds of activities and convergences.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, we will be informed by the general settings and requirements and make sure that these are observed rigorously.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, we are also working with, as I have said, MOH, NEA and BCA.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These are specialised agencies that have important perspectives that then informs the measures that we can take in Changi Airport, as necessary.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, let me assure Members that it is something that we are watching and monitoring closely and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect the health and safety of our workers.
